items.event_time_ist: Tuesday, Oct 13, 2026 (exact hour unverified; first reported ~5:46 PM IST)
items.summary: The Saudi-led coalition's joint forces command ordered civilians to evacuate the Yemen Oil Company's Sabah (Al-Sabahah) central fuel station in Sanaa on Tuesday, publishing a map of the site and saying to leave "for their own safety" ahead of a planned military operation (no timeline given). Spokesman Maj. Gen. Turki al-Malki announced it on X. In response, Houthi spokesman Yahya Saree warned that any strike on Sanaa would draw a "harsh and painful" response in Riyadh, and the Houthis told all employees and civilians at Saudi Aramco oil facilities to evacuate and stay away, declaring them "legitimate targets." (Also reported by AP, AFP via Mint, and Gulf Business.)
items.title: Coalition orders Sanaa fuel-site evacuation ahead of operation; Houthis threaten Riyadh retaliation, warn Aramco staff to evacuate

items.summary: Coalition spokesman Turki al-Malki said on X that Saudi forces shot down three drones over northern Riyadh on Tuesday, Oct 13; no attribution or damage detail given (also noted in Reuters' reporting). Same report adds: Houthi-run Al Masirah says coalition jets struck Saada province at least three times Tuesday morning after hitting northern/western areas overnight; Saree claims the Houthis downed a Saudi armed drone over Saada (unverified); and Yemen's government says Taiz clashes continued through the morning with fighter jets hitting rebel facilities nine times.
items.title: Coalition says it downed 3 drones over northern Riyadh on Tuesday; Saada hit overnight, Taiz fighting continues
